verdicts.rewritten_summary: Outright International country profile (updated Mar 2026): same-sex conduct criminalised since the colonial era; the 2014 'aggravated homosexuality' life clause was removed by the March 2025 Criminal Code, which instead sets a five-year minimum for 'unnatural offences' (defined as any homosexual act) with no stated maximum, plus three years for 'gross indecency'; the Barrow government has not typically enforced the provisions.

West Africa Democracy Radio: reports The Gambia's new criminal-law package raising the minimum sentence for homosexual acts to five years — broadcast corroboration of the penalty change now on the books.

Freedom House, Freedom in the World 2024: The Gambia rated 'Partly Free' (50/100); political freedoms improved under Barrow after 22 years of Jammeh's rule, with severe discrimination against LGBT+ people listed among ongoing concerns.

UK Home Office CPIN on sexual orientation and gender identity in Gambia (v3.0, Feb 2023): systematic assessment of risk, protection, internal relocation and certification for LGBT+ asylum claims, with detailed country information on law and treatment — the fullest English-language documentation of conditions on the ground.

HRW report 'State of Fear' (Sept 2015): arbitrary arrests, torture and killings in Gambia under Jammeh, including his anti-gay rhetoric and explicit threats against LGBT people — the enforcement climate of the previous regime, relevant to how police treat visibly LGBT visitors.
US State Dept 2020 human-rights report on Gambia: same-sex conduct criminalised (up to life under the 2013 amendment); documents arrests and societal discrimination.
US State Dept 2021 report: continued criminalisation with no prosecutions reported; significant societal stigma and police harassment of LGBT persons.

US State Dept 2012 report on Guinea-Bissau: documents the 2012 coup, arbitrary killings, torture, drug-trafficking-linked corruption and impunity; notes no criminalisation of same-sex conduct — general security context for visitors.
US State Dept 2011 report: security-force torture, FGM and impunity documented; the LGBT section notes no criminalisation but societal stigma against LGBT people.

Overview of LGBT rights in Guinea-Bissau: same-sex conduct legal since 1993 (penal code decree 4/93 omits same-sex offences); signed the 2008 UN SOGI statement; only married heterosexual couples entitled to larger government housing; domestic-violence law (6/2014) Article 5 protects victims regardless of sexual orientation.

Mapa.gay country guide for Guinea-Bissau: legal since 1993; no partnership recognition; no trans framework; travel-safety score 34/100 ('Caution'); 9% consider homosexual behaviour morally acceptable — unusually moderate for West Africa; no visible LGBT scene; some violence cases (2018).

Synergía IHR report on lesbophobia, human rights and police raids in Equatorial Guinea: police and military intervene in spaces of assembly, expression and residence of lesbian women; in Bata, police detain known lesbians collectively ('lesbians are members of a sect'), including collective punishment when one lesbian is sought.

Outright International profile (updated Mar 2026): the 2022 penal code does not explicitly criminalise same-sex intimacy or gender diversity, but a 2020 Draft Law 'Regulating Prostitution and the Rights of Homosexuals' (status unclear) would effectively criminalise; authorities still apply the obsolete 1954 Law on Vagrants and Criminals, which normalises conversion practices and classifies homosexuality as illness; three instruments institutionalise discrimination (Military Justice Code, ministerial order on 'immoral' activities, provincial regulation).
US State Dept 2021 report: same-sex conduct not specifically criminalised but LGBT persons face societal stigma; no anti-discrimination protections, within general repression context.
thin: no usable finding

UPR stakeholder submission (Small Media, EG Justice, IPI, Digital Rights in Equatorial Guinea) for the country's fourth UN review: freedom of expression, digital rights and journalist safety — documents the repressive environment that also constrains LGBT advocacy.

Hispanic Studies Review (Oct 2025): academic analysis of queer motherhood in Equatoguinean novelist Trifonia Melibea Obono's 'Yo no quería ser madre' (2019) — compulsory heterosexuality and queer invisibility as social-climate context.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024): marriage-equality Law 5089/2024 added SOGIESC equal-treatment guarantees in goods/services, education, healthcare and housing; in March a mob of ~150 attacked two trans people in Thessaloniki (21 arrested, 11 minors) followed by a masked attack on counter-protesters; the Orthodox Church officially opposed marriage equality; transphobic comments targeted Eurovision contestants.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025): the ECtHR condemned Greece for detaining an LGBTI Iranian refugee pending deportation (Article 3 violation); a criminal case opened over an online post inciting discrimination against immigrants and LGBTI people; in July the Crete Court of Appeal convicted three French tourists for a 2017 attack.

ECtHR app. 459/16, Koutra and Katzaki v. Greece (judgment 2017): police stopped and mistreated transgender sex workers and their lawyer in Athens in 2013 (street stops, removal from cars); complaints against officers were discontinued — documented police conduct toward visibly trans people.

PinkNews (Apr 2024): the UK Foreign Office updated its Greece travel advice for LGBTQ+ holidaymakers — same-sex relations legal, civil unions since 2015, marriage since Feb 2024 (first Orthodox-majority country), age of consent 15 for all, legal gender change possible; travellers advised to remain alert.

EU FRA LGBTIQ survey III, Greece country sheet (2024): 63% avoid holding hands with a same-sex partner (EU-27: 53%); 36% avoid certain locations for fear of assault (EU: 29%); only 35% are open about being LGBTIQ (EU: 51%); 28% felt discriminated at work (EU: 19%).

Outright profile (updated Mar 2026): Greece ranked 7th in Europe on the 2025 Rainbow Map; conversion practices banned for minors and IGM criminalised (2022); employment-discrimination ban on SOGI (2023); Feb 2024 Law 5089/2024 extended equal-treatment grounds (SOGIESC) across social protection, education, healthcare, housing and goods/services alongside marriage equality.

The Press Project (May 2025): TGEU Trans Rights Index & Map 2025 shows backsliding outpacing progress across Europe for the first time; Greece meets 21 of 32 indicators — gaps include age restrictions on name changes, no national action plan, no legal recognition of trans/non-binary parenthood.

Wikipedia overview: same-sex marriage legal since 2024; adoption and foster care; discrimination and hate-speech protections; self-ID gender recognition since 2017; conversion therapy; military service; social conditions including Pride events and homophobic violence.

PinkNews (Apr 2008): Justice Ministry pledged a working group on cohabiting gay couples' rights feeding upcoming unmarried-couples legislation — historical context only; superseded by civil unions (2015) and marriage equality (Feb 2024).

The Advocates for Human Rights + Khaleem Ali + GrenCHAP UPR stakeholder report (Oct 2024) on LGBTIQ+ rights in Grenada: documents the legal and social situation for the UN review, including Sections 430/431 criminal provisions, and GrenCHAP's 15+ years of service to marginalised groups (LGBT+, PLHIV, sex workers, vulnerable youth).

Outright International profile (updated Mar 2026): same-sex conduct criminalised under Sections 430 ('grossly indecent act') and 431 ('unnatural crime'); no legal gender recognition; no anti-discrimination protections; LGBTIQ people face discrimination in housing, education, employment and public services, and fear of prosecution inhibits reporting to police.

US State Dept 2023 report on Grenada: significant human-rights issues include laws criminalising consensual sexual conduct between men, though not enforced; no arbitrary killings, torture or disappearances reported.

GlobalGayz 'Gay Greenland - Past and Present' (May 2015): gay life is 'almost a non-event' — low-key, integrated, non-violent; modest Pride march since 2010; the 1996 same-sex partnership law passed with virtually no debate — a picture of quiet tolerance.

PinkNews (Apr 2016): Greenland's same-sex marriage law came into effect — adopted Danish legislation, passed unanimously twice (first bill lapsed due to Danish elections); replaces the 1996 partnership law; the established church's bishop supported it.

KNR Greenlandic Broadcasting (Aug 2014): new national association LGBT Qaamaneq founded for lesbians, gays, bisexuals and transgender people — political, cultural and social equality, open to family, friends and colleagues as supporters.

Wikipedia article on transfemicide: documents killings of trans women; for Guatemala records that Central American governments have long excluded trans women from femicide protections — Guatemalan officials have justified this by stating that transgender women are not 'biological women' — the official exclusion underpinning the record's violence context.

Arcus Foundation report (May 2024): the Inter-American Court's 2017 gender-identity opinion (Advisory Opinion OC-24/17) advanced legal gender recognition in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, but a vociferous opposition movement defining gender in strictly binary terms is fomenting backlash in all four countries.

HRW (Jan 2022): 'Guatemala: Anti-Trans Bill Threatens Rights' — documents legislative attacks on trans people, including bills that would erase gender identity protections and restrict legal recognition.

Washington Blade (Jan 2018): Latin American countries including Guatemala urged to abide by the Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruling (Advisory Opinion OC-24/17) requiring marriage equality and gender recognition — compliance status uncertain.

BuzzFeed News feature (Jan 2018): trans women in France incarcerated on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area — practice that applies in French Guiana as a French overseas region applying French law.
CGLPL opinion (25 May 2021) on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations persist across French places of detention, applicable in French Guiana.

Grokipedia page on transgender rights in French Guiana: France's national framework applies — simplified legal gender recognition since 2017 (administrative declaration, no surgery/sterilisation/diagnosis), anti-discrimination protections since 2012, hate-crime provisions 2017; specialised trans healthcare limited by remoteness; societal transphobia and cultural taboos discourage visibility and reporting.
